audit.why: 51.12% over 223 games with a lane Kennen owns from 2 to first item and Ryze reclaims at two mana items — EVEN 5.5/10 describes that curve accurately, and the mirror changed only the chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Skill at Levels 4-5 and Level 6 and Kennen at 2+ items. The packet says Kennen for 4-5 and 6, Ryze at 2+ items, and the mirror already applied exactly that.
audit.why: Levels 4-6 are Kennen's poke-and-kite window plus Slicing Maelstrom; whys[6] on this very page already argues Ryze wins at two mana items, so the chart contradicted its own caption.
audit.corrected: phases[3]/win[3] and phases[4]/win[4] Skill -> Kennen; phases[6]/win[6] Kennen -> Ryze with rating 5/10 -> 7/10. Proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Lightning Surge' is fabricated — it appears in spikes[1] and mid. Kennen's R is Slicing Maelstrom and his E is Lightning Rush. spikes[1] also claims the R 'pulls him into you'; it has no pull, it is a 550-range storm around him.
audit.why: Riot text: Slicing Maelstrom summons a storm striking nearby champions, 120s flat, 550 range. Lightning Rush is the 170-range lightning form (10/9/8/7/6) that lets him pass through units — that is how he closes the gap the storm needs.
audit.corrected: Real names used, the pull claim killed, and the actual mechanic stated: he cannot stun you with R unless Lightning Rush covers the distance first, so hold spacing of wave-width plus Phase Rush while the flat 120s is up.

audit.whatIsWrong: No itemisation note for Kennen's on-hit damage.
audit.why: Electrical Surge applies on-hit and rides attack speed, so armour reads the trade wrong — magic resist is what changes it.

edits.before: Kennen's R is the biggest threat in the matchup — Lightning Surge pulls him into you and chains AoE stuns that delete your Phase Rush window before it procs.
edits.after: Slicing Maelstrom is the biggest threat here — a flat 120s storm reaching only 550, so he needs Lightning Rush to close first; punish the approach, not the storm.

edits.before: Use Lightning Rush (E) to close through your W root attempt and trigger his AOE stun before Phase Rush saves you
edits.after: Close with Lightning Rush, 10s at rank 1, and land the third Mark of the Storm before Phase Rush carries you clear

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are Kennen's entire window and he knows it. He plays Phase Rush chicken with you — he pokes, you proc Phase Rush to disengage, he resets and pokes again. The mana drain is real: do NOT dump Rune Prison as poke, keep it strictly for his Lightning Rush engage or a gank setup. At 6 his R becomes the matchup-defining cooldown: a full-commit Lightning Surge into R stuns you through Phase Rush if he closes before it procs, so the moment his R comes off cooldown your positioning has to be wave-width plus your Phase Rush distance — if he cannot close that gap he cannot stun you. Track his R cooldown obsessively and use his downtime to shove the wave and bank Manaflow stacks.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are Kennen's entire window and he knows it. He plays Phase Rush chicken with you — he pokes, you proc Phase Rush to disengage, he resets and pokes again. The mana drain is real: do NOT dump Rune Prison as poke, keep it strictly for his Lightning Rush engage, 10 seconds at rank 1, or for a gank setup. At 6 Slicing Maelstrom becomes the matchup-defining cooldown: a flat 120 seconds reaching only 550, so he must cover the gap with Lightning Rush first. The moment his R is up your spacing has to be wave-width plus your Phase Rush distance — if he cannot cover that, he cannot stun you. Shove and bank Manaflow stacks through the downtime.

edits.before: After Seraph's Embrace your combo loop runs fast enough that a single W root into Flux-empowered Q chain threatens to delete him — he has no reliable answer to being rooted in melee range. The game plan becomes disciplined: never walk up without Phase Rush ready, hold W for his Lightning Rush engage rather than spending it as poke, and look for Realm Warp flanks that bring your team onto him at angles his kite speed cannot escape. He retains move-speed advantage in open fights, so the winning pattern is always root first, then chain — never auto-commit from range and hope he stands still.
edits.after: After Seraph's Embrace your loop runs fast enough that one Rune Prison into a Flux-empowered Overload chain threatens to delete him — he has no answer to being rooted at 615. The plan is disciplined: never walk up without Phase Rush ready, hold W for his Lightning Rush engage rather than spending it as poke, and take Realm Warp flanks that land your team on him at angles his move speed cannot escape. Electrical Surge applies on-hit and his damage rides attack speed, so armour reads the trade wrong — magic resist is the stat that changes it. Root first, then chain.

notes: 'Lightning Surge' is a fabricated ability name that appeared twice; Kennen's R is Slicing Maelstrom and it does not pull — it is a 550-range storm on a flat 120s, which changes the counterplay from 'dodge the ult' to 'deny Lightning Rush the gap'. Level chart rows 4-5, 6 and 2+ items flipped in matched pairs to agree with the packet and the mirror. On-hit itemisation (magic resist, not armour) added to late.
